reviews.title: Outstanding performance, but mounting system needs refinement
reviews.comment:
The Arctic Liquid Freezer III Pro 360 is keeping my Ryzen 9 9900X exceptionally cool. Under controlled 24‑thread stress testing—including sustained AVX/matrix workloads—the CPU holds around 62 °C, which is excellent for a processor of this class. In real‑world workloads like photo & video upscaling, batch video encodes and large software builds, I typically see temperatures in the mid to high 60s and occasional spikes into the 70s, which is completely normal for the 9900X and still well within comfortable thermal limits. I've also observed idle temperatures as low as 35c, but they usually sit between 36-39c.
The pump is very quiet, the radiator fans move a lot of air without excessive noise, and overall thermal stability has been outstanding.
Installation was mostly smooth, but the CPU block mounting system needs refinement. Once the mounting brackets were secured to the motherboard, they ended up just a little too close together, which meant the two screws on the CPU block didn’t line up with their holes. I had to loosen the bracket screws, mount the block, then retighten everything. It worked, but it shouldn’t require that workaround. I also wish the block used four mounting screws instead of two for more even pressure.
Despite that hiccup, the cooling performance is exceptional, and once installed, the unit has been rock‑solid. For high‑core‑count CPUs like the Ryzen 9 9900X, this AIO has more than enough thermal headroom for both synthetic stress tests and demanding real‑world workloads.

reviews.title: Great Cooler But Buy Thermal Paste
reviews.comment:
This is the second ARCTIC cooler I have purchased with the first being the Freezer II. I think it is a fantastic product. The price is great and it cools wonderfully. However, the thermal paste with both coolers was dried out. I went from idle temps being 40 even 50 C and fans annoyingly loud to 29C and fans quiet. Gaming was a big difference going from upper 80C to 60C. I am unsure why I had bad luck with the paste, but I would recommend this product regardless.
Installation has even gotten easier and the RGB is pretty if that is your sort of thing. It fit my case, but it is a snug fit at the top of a Montech AIR 903 MAX. It seemed easier to mount this one than my other cooler and the screws was fairly easy to screw in unlike the last cooler I had.
It is a hefty cooler and I think it will hold up nicely. The magnetic CPU fan is interest and simple to install. The RGB part does not spin so don't worry about that as the fan itself is underneath that.
reviews.author: Kay M.

reviews.title: Excellent AIO cooler for Ryzen 5800x3D!
reviews.comment: Purchased for 5800x3d and I couldn't be happier. My previous AIO pump is assumed stopped working. And during games would sit at 91c. Assuming due to the CPU throttling. So I was not getting full power. Decided to replace it eith this one based on online recommendations and reciews. I could nor my CPU could not be happier. Now my CPU never goes over 70c. It runs at full clock speeds, including boost. I did personally undervolt the CPU with curve to keep my clock speeds. But it runs flawlessly! Couldn't recommend a better AIO cooler. And it works with Intel, and both AMD sockets (AM4 and AM5). The size is huge, make sure you do research to make sure it fits in your case/motherboard. For me, I use Lian Li Dynamic 011 Razer Edition with Gigabyte z570s Aurora ELITE AX. And I have room to push pull setup. Installation was not difficult with the videos from Arctic YouTube channel. Does not come with instructions. I did upgrade the Termal paste as well as suggested. I went with Corsair xtm70 instead.

reviews.title: Excellent cooler for AM4, but buy your own thermal paste!!
reviews.comment:
The media could not be loaded.  https://m.media-amazon.com/images/I/D1jcvOUaIEL.mp4 https://m.media-amazon.com/images/I/712G0Y4zw9L._SY256.jpg *Update*: RGB works flawlessly
GREAT product for AM4 CPU's.
I have been looking to replace my aging Corsair H100i Pro AIO, which I bought in 2019, for some time now. After I read all the glowing reviews, I was really excited to get this cooler. I did not see many reviews from folks with AM4 processors, though, so I was a little bit wary, especially when the instructions said not to worry about some of the chip being visible after install! D:
I need not have worried. This cooler dropped temps about ~14 degrees C across the board. Went from 80 degrees under load to 66! Idle went from 50 to 36. For reference, I have an AMD R9 5900x, one of the hotter-running AM4 chips. Also I do have PBO enabled! (check screenshot for temp/load details).
As others have stated, the radiator on this unit is quite large/thick, so make sure to measure your case to make sure there is room to accommodate it. My mid-tower case is old, but quite roomy, so I luckily had no trouble fitting it in my case. It is also significantly louder than my old two-fan cooler, but its not even as loud as my GPU, so I am not particularly bothered. Others may be, though, so you may want to modify your fan speed curve.
Installation was not particularly difficult, and did not take much time. I found instructions using the QR code on the box (click on the 'Manuals' tab), and they were more than adequate. They included some graphics, gifs, and videos. I have a few decades of exp building PC's, so take this with a grain of salt, but I think beginners will not have too much trouble with this install. The trickiest part was removing the standard AM4 mount brackets and installing the ones included with the cooler. I had to hold the backplate (on the back of mobo) with one hand, while I installed the brackets one screw at a time. Bit of a pain, but the results were worth it.
The only (and biggest) con, is that the MX-6 thermal paste included with the cooler had the consistency of silly putty. It was basically a solid. Seeing as the 8G MX-6 tube I bought, to replace the minuscule amount that arrived with the cooler, had a more viscous consistency, I assume it was a bad batch. This delayed my build by a period of two days (while waiting for thermal paste to arrive), and is the only reason why I am giving this product 4 stars instead of 5.
I have not tested ARGB functionality, since I do not have a header on my old X570 motherboard, but I have ordered a header for it, and will update this review once it arrives.
In short: buy this cooler for sure. Great value for money, and incredible performance. But!! Make sure to order your own thermal paste, because they may include Playdough in the box instead of actual thermal paste D:
